Authority & Stop Rules

Courses teach the material. Each task tells you what to learn, what to do, and the exact condition for marking it done. No separate proof-writing task is required.
Authority
1.
This catalogue is the only operational calendar.
2.
The three July 2026 MD reports control the umbrella direction and learning order. Current priority is the umbrella stack first, UAE employment second; Vancouver applications remain a small deadline-driven background track.
3.
DUBAI_PLAN.pdf contributes execution patterns only: honest project ownership, interview honesty and re-angle-not-restart. Its expired trip, visa, AWS-first, bridge-project and eight-week assumptions do not control this plan.
4.
This HTML is the execution layer: it may sequence and test the MD goals, but it may not silently replace them with an older specialization.
5.
Reverify official vacancies, university rules, exam details, immigration rules and deadlines before paying or submitting.
6.
Only the next 14 days need exact placement. Later work stays inside broad phases until it becomes relevant.
Workload rules
Start at roughly 22 focused hours per week. Earn any increase through four weeks of finished work, not optimism. After full-time employment, switch immediately to a reduced role-first schedule.
Only the next 14 days become ready. Later tasks stay weekly, and unselected branches create no tasks. Previous course percentages or AI-assisted output do not prove completion.
Do not create standalone “exit” exercises just to prove a completed course. Independence is checked where it matters: building, debugging, changing and explaining the real backend project or handling an actual interview-style task.
Re-angle; do not restart. No new course, certification, language, project, or planner redesign enters the active plan unless a current task, verified employer response, or confirmed programme requirement creates the need.
DSA is mandatory, not a gate in front of backend work. Once SQL/PostgreSQL is usable, HTTP and FastAPI may proceed while DSA continues in parallel. Do not delay employer-visible backend evidence just to finish every algorithm lesson first.
Daily Coding Gym is exactly that: coding practice, six days per week. It uses only Boot.dev Training Grounds, LeetCode and Codewars. No CV work, project tickets, repository defence, application activity, evidence logging or planner bureaucracy lives in this ritual layer. The progression is deliberate: implementation fluency before DSA, learned-topic LeetCode once Boot.dev DSA begins, harder kata and approachable Mediums after DSA1, then LeetCode 75 / timed interview practice after DSA2. Sunday is the same-week catch-up day only: missed Coding Gym sessions from Monday–Saturday can be recovered there, and nothing carries into the next Monday.
Course-first rule. Boot.dev remains the source of new DSA concepts. The Coding Gym only drills skills already learned. During each timed rep, do the work yourself first; solution/editorial review happens only after the active timebox.
The UAE search starts selectively now. In the current graduate-baseline tier, send roughly 2–3 highly qualified applications per week using only evidence you can defend today. Technical learning/building remains the majority of the workload. The Applications page widens role families and raises the target only when SQL/PostgreSQL, HTTP/FastAPI, tested backend work, Docker/CI/public release and AWS evidence actually become true. Week 6 / 31 August is a systematic-search checkpoint, not a permission date.
Explicitly skipped or postponed
Active structured courses and exact Boot.dev modules are sticky on Today. Boot.dev now uses exact published chapter/lesson tasks: the current module appears no earlier than its planned target date and then stays visible every day until checked; the next module waits for its own target date. Udemy, Talk Python and GitHub Skills multi-day course/exercise blocks remain sticky as before. For the DSA + PostgreSQL parallel lane, Today keeps both active surfaces visible; for true multi-day blocks it still computes a progress-aware daily target: DSA keeps a protected primary floor, PostgreSQL keeps a protected secondary floor, and neither lane can consume the other. Finish faster and later work remains upcoming until its target date; fall behind and the unfinished work carries forward visibly as Delayed without rewriting its original target date. The displayed block hours remain total estimates, not a daily quota.
Course-first rule: the planner sequences learning; real courses teach it. Remaining Boot.dev courses now use one dated task per official chapter. Today shows the exact named chapter due that day; Boot.dev chapter completion, not logged minutes, is the progress signal. Boot.dev Learn SQL is now complete and remains the SQL-language foundation. Comparing the current Boot.dev syllabus against Stephen Grider’s SQL/PostgreSQL course shows heavy overlap in Grider Sections 3–5 and 9–11, so they remain skipped by default. The useful remainder is tracked as six conceptual developer blocks rather than one planner task per Udemy section: bridge/local environment; application schema/integrity; relational modelling; performance/query tools; transactions/migrations; and application integration/security/testing. Recursive CTEs and materialized views remain optional unless a real project need appears; Section 37 is not planner work. DSA starts in parallel. After DSA 1 Chapter 4 — Sorting Algorithms, HTTP can begin while the remaining DSA chapters and PostgreSQL continue independently. POSTGRES-SCHEMA still applies the PostgreSQL type/constraint/design material after Section 15; later Grider sections reinforce the same backend rather than blocking it.
↔
Source-track note. The planner keeps the .md research destination and required skill stack. Three timing choices are explicit employment-driven overrides rather than claims that the reports prescribed them: HTTP/FastAPI starts after the real DSA 1 Chapter 4 gate, before all DSA chapters are finished; selective truthful UAE applications start from the current graduate baseline rather than waiting for the full backend release; routine Canada preparation stays deferred to the October portal/deadline window. The public project still marks the point where backend applications become substantially stronger and broader. DSA, Docker/CI/AWS, the six-program admissions basket and the later overlay remain retained.
Do not start Functional Programming, AI Agent, Static Site Generator, Memory Management, JavaScript, TypeScript, Go, RAG or another backend language before the job-ready release unless a real assessment or employer requirement changes the plan.
Project One remains a bounded career-pipeline API. No payments, multi-tenancy, billing, microservices, Kubernetes, multiple providers or large frontend are required for the umbrella goal.
Do not revive the old dissertation or a synthetic CLI as a second build lane. Project One remains the single active portfolio build. The original dissertation refresh moves into Week 4 and becomes Module 1 of the bounded hybridAUTH interview-defence syllabus; Modules 2–3 use the remaining Week 4 capacity, Module 4 uses Week 5 capacity, and Modules 5–7 are woven into the original tested-backend, project-defence and shipped-project review checkpoints. Do not redeploy, rewrite or turn hybridAUTH into recurring weekly development.
Pandas and machine learning begin only through the selected April–May overlay. The data branch is a connected data-contract, idempotent-ingestion and SQL-first analytics extension; an interpretable model and MLOps-lite evidence appear only when their trigger is real. Airflow, Spark, Kafka, warehouses, Kubernetes, feature stores and registry platforms stay deferred.
Cloud Practitioner is only an optional quick signal after the AWS course and labs; Developer Associate follows real deployment and operations only when market value justifies it; ISC2 CC exists only for a rising cyber branch. Deferring every certificate is valid.
Formal transcript-bearing maths/statistics remediation outranks vendor badges whenever a retained programme confirms a credit prerequisite.

Decision Branches

The umbrella core stays active
Python, Linux, Git/GitHub, SQL/PostgreSQL, DSA, HTTP/API design, FastAPI, pytest/QA work, secure defaults, Docker, CI and AWS are the shared spine. Linux is already complete; weaknesses discovered in the real project or job process create targeted repair work, not standalone exit exams.
At most one light overlay
After the cloud-ready release and two job-funnel reviews, activate at most one bounded cyber, data/ML, deeper software/cloud or employed-maintenance branch—or choose none. Re-angle the current role search before adding a specialization. The data/ML option additionally requires confirmed maths/prerequisite requirements, an obtainable dataset and a five-week release contract. All other overlays remain absent.
Certifications come after hands-on work
Certificates ratify hands-on work; they do not replace it. AWS Cloud Practitioner is an optional quick signal only after the Boot.dev AWS course and AWS labs. AWS Developer – Associate is the stronger backend/cloud credential and stays locked until Project One is deployed and operated on AWS. LFCS is optional only if Linux-heavy backend/support/cloud roles become a real target. Do not add PostgreSQL, Python, Docker or QA certificates by default.
Programme applications are conditional
BCIT Applied Computing, UBC MEng ECE, SFU Cybersecurity, SFU Visual Computing, SFU Big Data and UBC MDS create application tasks only after live eligibility, prerequisite, affordability and cycle checks pass. UBC MEL remains watchlist-only while paused or experience-ineligible.
Employer funnel: re-angle, do not restart
Use repeated employer signal to change positioning, not one rejection. Backend/Python traction means stay the course. QA automation, application support or cloud/platform traction means re-angle the same umbrella toward that role family. If data-oriented engineering roles clearly outperform after enough real applications, the later data overlay may be considered. If nothing responds, diagnose eligibility, CV top-third, project proof and targeting before buying another course.
↔
What never happens here: one quiet week does not trigger a new language, new certification, new portfolio identity or new master plan.
15 June 2027 route decision
Compare real UAE employment results with admissions, programme fit, total cost, funding, current immigration facts and start dates. Activate exactly one employment, study-transition or continued-search route.
Re-angle the existing stack before restarting. No new giant project, second certification, language, or planner redesign may postpone a decision the real options already make clear.

How a learning module closes

Settings

Backup, restore & delete
Everything (settings, tasks, applications, optional notes, branch state, and completion history) lives in localStorage under hamza-master-execution-v2. This section gives you a real full-state backup and restore path for GitHub Pages: export JSON, import that JSON later, or deliberately wipe this browser's saved copy.
🧯
Do not rely on browser storage alone. Export occasionally after major progress or before resetting. Restoring replaces the entire planner state with the imported JSON. Delete/reset actions are irreversible unless you exported first.
Deploy on GitHub Pages
1.
Save this file as index.html in a new repo (e.g. hamza-execution-planner).
2.
Push to GitHub. Settings → Pages → deploy from main / root.
3.
Live at https://<you>.github.io/hamza-execution-planner/.
4.
Bookmark on phone & desktop. Each device's data is independent — use Export/Import to sync.
